page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfr6.4xlarge consistently in the average performance tier. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1436.39, while the multi-core score reaches 15326.6. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 853.84 GB/sec, which drops to 90.41 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 49.06 GB/sec. In application-specific benchmarks, the server handles 14.91 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 12.32 GB/sec. For language model tasks, prompt processing with a small 135M model reaches 937.39 tokens/sec, but performance drops to a weak 23.2 tokens/sec when processing prompts for a medium 7B model.

Given its dedicated Intel Xeon processor and high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.hfr6.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of local storage or GPU hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for flexible network storage configurations. This profile is appropriate for database operations, caching layers like Redis, memory-intensive web serving, and software compilation tasks, as evidenced by its Passmark database score of 5955.88 and Geekbench software compilation score of 13822.0.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.4xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It operates on a KVM hypervisor with no local storage or GPUs, utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average performance across most metrics, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15326.6 and a Passmark CPU score of 16780.3. The instance demonstrates solid memory performance, delivering 14.91 million Redis SET operations per second and a cached read bandwidth of 853.84 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in complex tasks, such as prompt processing for 7B LLM models, which registers at 23.2 tokens/sec. This server is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching applications that do not require local NVMe storage.
